title: Agentic Engineering Golden Standard
subtitle: A practical field guide for engineering value and independent mastery

pages.title: How the standard works
pages.intro: Use this standard to choose valuable work, deliver a small verified improvement, and learn the engineering well enough to reproduce and defend it yourself. The maintained product is this reusable workflow and learning system.

rows: Observed task volume, active labor, review, rework and support. Distinguish released capacity from cash savings.
Executed tests, negative cases, source revisions, measured limits and independent review of consequential claims.
Unaided coding or debugging, an architecture defense and a new transfer case. AI-assisted work is recorded separately.

blocks.heading: What the repository contains
blocks.body: OpenCode helpers, engineering rules, templates, eight learning modules and dependency-free synthetic reference code. Its current maturity is L1: local reference checks. Version 2 does not mean enterprise production readiness.

blocks.heading: What you supply in a company
blocks.body: A bounded approved task, source owners, real identity and authorization, domain validators, operating ownership and a usable employee workflow. The repository provides no production executor, company approvals, live model or employee application.

blocks.title: Start here
blocks.body: Read pages 1-3 for the operating model, 4-8 for design and value, 9-10 for daily and offline use, and 11-12 for interview preparation. The guide explains canonical rules; its source list on every page tells you where the full rule lives.

pages.title: Run one bounded change
pages.intro: Each iteration produces a reviewable result and a learning artifact. Specify acceptance before writing code; preserve working architecture and model settings.

blocks.heading: A synthetic example
blocks.body: A search result incorrectly boosts JOB-1 when the query asks for JOB-10. Reproduce the failure, define token-equality acceptance, make the small fix and rerun regressions. Then independently explain tokenization, ranking cost and why the toy role filter is not authentication.

blocks.title: Finish honestly
blocks.body: Report verified behavior, exact tests, unverified integrations, measurements and one next task. A merged PR is software evidence; it is not proof that the human mastered the code.

pages.title: Keep authority outside the model
pages.intro: Separate the engineering assistant, the application runtime and company-controlled execution. The model can propose; trusted code and accountable people enforce the boundaries.

blocks.heading: Model workflow and agent
blocks.body: A language model generates outputs from context. A fixed workflow runs known steps. An agent uses model decisions and tool feedback to choose its next step within a bounded goal. Retrieval supplies evidence; it does not make the model authoritative. Keep deterministic work deterministic, and add dynamic decisions only when they help.

items: OpenCode and approved model -> code, tests, reviewable PR
Trusted identity -> scoped evidence/tools -> reasoning -> validators
Separate authenticated approval and controlled handoff; no direct model write path

blocks.heading: The local teaching state machine
blocks.body: ChangeRun models created -> evidence_ready -> drafted -> validated -> reviewed -> exported. It rehashes the draft at gates. Reviewed is an unverified caller assertion; exported is a returned local copy. Fields and events remain mutable. There is no durable store, real approval, retry deduplication or audit-integrity guarantee.

blocks.heading: The target production contract
blocks.body: Task requests carry identity references, scope, budgets, deadlines and idempotency keys. Evidence carries revision, hash, permission scope and timestamps. Tool calls and traces bind approved definitions and policy decisions. Approval binds exact artifact, validator, reviewer, scope and expiry. Cancellation competes atomically with handoff.

blocks.title: Interview defense
blocks.body: Why does independent=True fail to prove reviewer independence? Why can a timeout mean an unknown remote outcome? Explain the transaction and trusted identity boundary before discussing more agents.

pages.title: Choose the smallest useful pattern
pages.intro: Start with deterministic lookup or retrieval. Add autonomy only for a demonstrated need, and measure the coordination overhead against the simpler baseline.

blocks.heading: Bound every design
blocks.body: Declare total step, tool, time and cost limits. Stop on policy denial, cancellation, deadline, exhausted budget or no progress. Examples in the pattern guide are starting limits, not universal SLOs. Durable execution can wrap any pattern without adding a model.

blocks.title: Decision to defend
blocks.body: State why your chosen pattern beats search, a script or a fixed workflow on the same cases. More agents are justified by observed benefit after coordination cost.

pages.title: Build context and govern tools
pages.intro: Retrieved material is evidence, even when it contains text pretending to be a system instruction. It cannot edit policy, tool definitions, permissions or workflow truth.

rows: Reviewed project/company policy; versioned and reconciled
Approved pinned publication; selected for the task
Authorized revision-pinned data; request-scoped and untrusted as instructions
Reviewed server and definition registry; minimal exposed operations
Trusted identity/policy service; checked per call, resume and output
Server-owned versioned checkpoint; model proposes transitions

blocks.heading: A definition hash needs a trusted baseline
blocks.body: Review descriptions and schemas before enrollment. Deny unknown servers/tools and definition drift. Check classification and approved model destination before disclosure. Keep secrets outside model context; enforce permissions again at the adapter and source. Tool annotations and retrieved commands do not authorize effects. MCP is a protocol for connecting tools and resources; it does not itself approve a server or grant business permissions.

blocks.title: What the offline tests establish
blocks.body: The policy example denies poisoned definitions, disallowed scope, classification, budget and canceled calls. It does not authenticate users, connect to MCP, execute tools or prove that a live model resists prompt injection.

pages.title: Measure the right kind of success
pages.intro: Separate contract correctness, retrieval, answer grounding, workflow completion and business impact. Success at one layer does not establish the next.

rows: Types, hashes, state order, scope and cancellation
Recall, precision, MRR and leakage by slice
Correct IDs do not prove correct claims
Claim correctness, citation support and revision
Needs labeled answers and calibrated graders
Safe completion, latency, recovery, tool usage/cost
Net active effort, quality, adoption and support

blocks.heading: A metric counterexample
blocks.body: Expected relevant IDs are A, B and C. Top three returned IDs are X, A and B. Recall@3 is 2/3, precision@3 is 2/3, reciprocal rank is 1/2. MRR averages reciprocal rank across answerable cases. Evaluate correct abstention separately for questions with no expected evidence.

blocks.heading: Know the provided evaluator
blocks.body: The seven original cases and 30 public domain-seed cases test tiny synthetic lexical retrieval. The legacy hit_at_k field combines a hit with correct abstention; it is not recall. The runner reports hashes, k, repeats and query-only p50/p95. No answer model runs; answer correctness, grounding and task success are unmeasured.

blocks.title: Evidence quality
blocks.body: Public fixtures are not protected holdouts. Repeated deterministic timing is not repeated model trials. Fresh holdouts require a separate curator; human/AI grading needs calibration. Report actual failures and provenance.

pages.title: Select work that repays its cost
pages.intro: Compare a small set of opportunities, including doing nothing and a deterministic improvement. Use a common horizon and label inputs measured, estimated or unknown.

blocks.heading: How the example works
blocks.body: 40 x (20 - 6 - 4 - 2) = 320 minutes/month before support. Subtract 120 support minutes: 200 net minutes/month. Build effort 480 / 200 = 2.4 months to break even, assuming stable demand and no other costs. First-month net after build is -280 minutes. These invented inputs illustrate arithmetic, not achieved ROI.

blocks.heading: Choose under uncertainty
blocks.body: Gate on authorization, safety, data and operating ownership. Compare conservative net benefit, time to evidence and maintenance burden. If unknown adoption changes the ranking, measure it first. Count review/rework once. Released capacity is not automatically cash saved. Yield or defect value requires independent attribution.

blocks.title: Interview defense
blocks.body: What assumption would reverse your recommendation? Why does an unknown cost differ from zero? What evidence would justify an agent over an approved export and a simple script?

pages.title: Adopt with limited IT support
pages.intro: Use what the organization can support. An approved versioned snapshot can test usefulness before a live connector. A shared service still needs real identity, permissions and an operator.

blocks.heading: Semiconductor example
blocks.body: On a synthetic source revision, investigate how sample_count flows through config, parser and validator. Cite exact revision and distinguish static evidence from unknown runtime dispatch. Compare two revisions and an override. This is an example for a separately authorized consuming application, not an assignment to build one in the standard.

blocks.heading: Transfer beyond manufacturing
blocks.body: For maintenance-manual search, preserve evidence revisions, authorization, uncertainty and evaluation. Change the task baseline, document owner and consequences of a wrong answer. Reuse contracts after validating the second setting; unobserved reuse is not realized business value.

blocks.title: Promotion requires evidence
blocks.body: Advance stages on observed quality, safe completion, sustainable support and net benefit. A passing local fixture never authorizes equipment, recipe, MES or production database writes.

pages.title: Find the right file and command
pages.intro: Keep the immutable reference snapshot separate from the application and from your learning records. Use canonical sources when a summary is not enough.

blocks.body: OpenCode needs approved tooling/model access. You can read the guide, run synthetic Python checks and do the exercises without it. Commands and skills never grant company permissions.

blocks.heading: What the preflight does
blocks.body: Checks the file manifest, structure/version/skill hashes, unit tests, both fixture sets and synthetic demos. It downloads nothing and invokes no model. A publisher-only packaging test may skip if Git is absent. Python itself, OpenCode, model weights, credentials and company integrations are not bundled.

blocks.heading: Understand the assurance
blocks.body: The ZIP names an exact committed snapshot. Checksums detect changes against a trusted expected value; they are not independent approval or publisher authentication. Windows execution is unverified until run on that PC. macOS and Linux CI results do not substitute for it.

blocks.title: If a prerequisite is blocked
blocks.body: Use approved internal provisioning or keep to reading and paper exercises. Preserve device controls and existing model settings. Detailed commands and brownfield steps are in OFFLINE_START.md.

pages.title: Build interview readiness through work
pages.intro: Target a role family, level and format. Keep a dated evidence index so you can see what is independent, assisted, stale or unassessed at any time.

rows: Explains with prompts/notes; cannot implement independently
Builds with AI; cannot reproduce independently yet
Unaided implementation/debugging plus adversarial tests and defense
Owns real release/support and measured impact; defends tradeoffs

blocks.heading: Build breadth with specific evidence
blocks.body: Applied agent roles emphasize bounded workflows and answer quality; platform/backend roles add concurrency and recovery; retrieval/evaluation roles add ground truth and uncertainty; security/reliability roles add abuse and fault diagnosis; technical leadership adds alternatives, ownership and adoption. Actual role requirements may add ML research, mathematics or accelerator infrastructure beyond this academy.

blocks.heading: A useful practice cadence
blocks.body: After a meaningful change, explain the mechanism, complete one unaided lab and defend a new failure case. Practice recall on days 2, 7 and 30. Suggested upkeep is a weekly mixed drill and monthly unseen coding/design assessment. These are local practice defaults, not a hiring guarantee.

blocks.title: Prepare an evidence packet
blocks.body: A 90-second project explanation, five-minute failure/tradeoff defense, executable unaided artifact and source-approved impact story. Keep company material inside approved systems; external career evidence needs appropriate approval.

pages.title: Complete your first unaided session
pages.intro: The first assessment observes validation, missing-evidence reasoning, testing and value judgment. It contains no generated solution and does not assign you a score.

blocks.heading: What the function must decide
blocks.body: Validate the exact synthetic input schema. Reject invalid known values before handling unknowns. Return insufficient_evidence when a field is unknown. Otherwise compute monthly net capacity and break-even, preserving zero/negative benefit. The full contract and public examples are in the assessment README.

blocks.heading: Checks are not the whole assessment
blocks.body: Visible tests let you self-check the contract. Independent mastery also requires observed unaided work, a new failure/transfer case and architecture defense. Record actual results in a dated copy of the readiness template. Next deeper lab: the SQLite retry, concurrency and cancellation exercise.

blocks.title: Explain this standard without notes
blocks.body: What do you choose before using an agent? Where does authority live? What proves an answer is grounded? Which cost could erase the benefit? What can you implement independently today? Use gaps to select the next standard improvement.
